description: PAIL (Physical Action Identity Layer) Core: an authorization and evidence layer for physical AI actions. A gate on the robot checks every command, such as a ROS 2 Twist on /cmd_vel, against a signed, single-use action token with named limits; unauthorized or out-of-bounds commands are refused with a reason code and not forwarded. Decisions go into a hash-chained journal that independent verifiers can check offline. Includes ROS 2 nodes, C ABI adapters, SDK, spec and test vectors.
rules: PAIL is an authorization and audit layer, not a safety system. Keep the robot's own safety functions and emergency stop in place; do not describe PAIL as a brake, speed limiter or safety controller.

Integrate on the command path: remap the base driver's input to /drive_cmd_vel and run pail_pep_gate and pail_motion_bridge in front of it, as in examples/tb3. A topic remap without SROS2 access control is not a barrier; the reference stack runs with SROS2 Enforce.

Do not clamp or rewrite commands to fit a limit. When the gate refuses a command, read the reason code and the named limit (for example ERR_ENVELOPE_EXCEEDED with step.max_duration_s) and submit a new plan within the limit.
Limits belong in the issuer's policy YAML, not in planner or application code. The planner does not need to change.

The Issuer in the evaluation bundle is a closed-source evaluation executable for internal non-production R&D and CI only. Production operation or redistribution requires a separate license from Glowfly Identity Systems (https://www.glowfly.ai).
Before using an evaluation bundle, check its SHA-256 and verify the manifest signature against the release key fingerprint published on the GitHub release page, as described in RELEASE.md.

Measured scope: simulated and raised-wheel TurtleBot3, Jetson Orin Nano Super (CPU) and Isaac Sim, as listed in README 'What has been measured'. Do not claim support for other robots, latency guarantees or functional-safety certification.
